Implementation: - Rule file `src/rules/require-branch-annotation.ts` exists and is explicitly tagged with this story: - JSDoc: `@story docs/stories/004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS.story.md`, `@req REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION`, `@req REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE`. - Exports a standard ESLint `RuleModule` with `meta.type = "problem"`, `meta.docs.description = "Require @story and @req annotations on code branches"`, `meta.messages.missingAnnotation = "Branch is missing required annotation: {{missing}}."`, and a schema describing the `branchTypes` option. - `create(context)` delegates to `validateBranchTypes(context)` and, for each configured branch type, registers a handler that calls `reportMissingAnnotations(context, node, storyFixCountRef)` (covering all configured "significant" branches).
Branch utilities and core behavior: - File `src/utils/branch-annotation-helpers.ts`: - `DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES` defines significant branches (REQ-BRANCH-DETECTION, REQ-SIGNIFICANCE-CRITERIA): `IfStatement`, `SwitchCase`, `TryStatement`, `CatchClause`, `ForStatement`, `ForOfStatement`, `ForInStatement`, `WhileStatement`, `DoWhileStatement`. - `validateBranchTypes(context)` (REQ-CONFIGURABLE-SCOPE): validates `options[0].branchTypes` against `DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES`. If invalid entries exist, returns a `Program` listener that reports: `Value "${t}" should be equal to one of the allowed values: ${DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES.join(", ")}`. Otherwise returns either the configured list or a copy of `DEFAULT_BRANCH_TYPES`. - `gatherBranchCommentText(sourceCode, node)` (REQ-COMMENT-ASSOCIATION): - For `SwitchCase`, scans up to 2 lines above the case for `//` or `/*` comments (handling the "blank line then comments" scenario). - For other nodes, uses `sourceCode.getCommentsBefore(node)` and concatenates comment text. - Internal `getBranchAnnotationInfo` (REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING): computes `missingStory`/`missingReq` via regex on gathered comment text, and computes indentation and insertion position via `sourceCode.getIndexFromLoc`. - `reportMissingStory` and `reportMissingReq` (REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING): - Report ESLint diagnostics with `messageId: "missingAnnotation"` and `data.missing` set to `"@story"` or `"@req"`. - Provide auto-fixers inserting `// @story .story.md` and `// @req ` above the branch; story fix limited via `storyFixCountRef.count`. - `reportMissingAnnotations(context, node, storyFixCountRef)` (REQ-ANNOTATION-PARSING, REQ-NESTED-HANDLING): uses `getBranchAnnotationInfo` to determine missing annotations and then iterates an `actions` array (for @story and @req) to report and fix as needed. This works uniformly for nested and top-level branches.
Integration into plugin configs: - `src/index.ts`: - `RULE_NAMES` includes `"require-branch-annotation"`, and rules are dynamically required from `./rules/${name}` so this rule is exported. - `TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES` maps `"traceability/require-branch-annotation"` to `"error"`. - `configs.recommended` and `configs.strict` are built from `TRACEABILITY_RULE_SEVERITIES`, so the rule is part of the main presets (DoD: rule integrated into presets).

traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria for story 004.0-DEV-BRANCH-ANNOTATIONS are met. The `require-branch-annotation` ESLint rule exists, enforces @story/@req annotations across a clearly defined and configurable set of branch node types, and includes logic for associating comments with branches and parsing annotations. It is implemented using standard ESLint RuleModule patterns with meta, schema, and message definitions, and is integrated into the plugin’s recommended and strict configurations.
Tests based on ESLint RuleTester cover both valid and invalid scenarios for all major branch constructs (if, switch, try/catch/finally, and all key loop types), including edge cases like blank lines before switch cases and configuration errors from invalid `branchTypes`. Error messages are clear and parameterized (`missingAnnotation` with `{{missing}}`), and auto-fix behavior inserts template @story/@req annotations at appropriate locations.
Dedicated rule documentation and README references provide configuration instructions and annotated examples, satisfying the documentation acceptance criterion. Together, the implementation, tests, integration, and docs provide concrete evidence that this story’s requirements and acceptance criteria have been fully implemented.
